meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid Bijural Federal State - Quebec is a Civil Law jurisdiction for private law matters under the Civil Code of Quebec; federal corporate and securities law is Common Law based; the Quebec Business Corporations Act is a statutory civil law instrument with Common Law inspired remedies

Canada - People's Republic of China Income Tax Agreement (1986), as amended by the 2010 Protocol
Canada - United States Income Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the 1983, 1995, 1997 and 2007 Protocols
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force July 1, 2020, including the Digital Trade chapter
Canada - European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisional application since September 21, 2017
Canada - United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (2021)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les societes par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 57-66 (register of ultimate beneficiaries maintained at registered office); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Loi sur la publicite legale des entreprises), CQLR c P-44.1, as amended by SQ 2022 c 15 (mandatory UBO declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec since March 31, 2023); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and FINTRAC regulations; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director, incorporator, and ultimate beneficial owner holding at least 25% of voting rights or fair market value of shares
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in country of origin; certified copy executed by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the origin state (e.g., PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs since November 7, 2023); consular legalization at a Canadian consulate for non-Apostille Convention states; certified French translation required for Quebec filings and bank KYC

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate shareholder or corporate ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country company registry (e.g., State Administration for Market Regulation in PRC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the home-country competent authority; certified French/English translation by an OCTAQ-certified translator or by a member of the Chambre des notaires du Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address and source-of-funds bank reference letter for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank and notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified French translation required by Canadian banking institutions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate / certificate of no criminal record for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent police or judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified French translation required by the receiving bank and registered-agent due diligence team

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO register declarations under the QBCA and initial director consent/resolution appointing the registered office in Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization in Quebec; no apostille required for documents executed and used entirely within Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against Global Affairs Canada Canadian Sanctions consolidated list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, and the OFAC SDN list (prudent standard given USD-denominated AdMob and AppLovin payouts routed through US-based payment processors). Enhanced due diligence applies to Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) with a five-year post-office cooling-off window. FINTRAC MSB registration is not required for the hyper-casual game publishing entity itself; however, the acquiring banks, payout platforms, and the corporation's Canadian bank will apply CDD/EDD under the PCMLTFA framework, requiring current, authenticated UBO documentation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online services portal https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; federal alternative for federal incorporation: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada portal at https://corporationscanada.ic.gc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French-language corporate name under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11; a common-law (English) name may be registered only if the French version is of equal or greater prominence and the corporation demonstrates a meaningful presence in Quebec; transliteration limited to Latin script; mandatory corporate suffix in French or English: Inc., Corp., Ltee, Corporation, Incorporee, or their written-out forms; the REQ requires a name that is distinctive, not misleading, and not contrary to public order under QBCA ss. 10-15 and LPLE ss. 23-24.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Bancaire - prior authorization of OSFI and the Autorite des marches financiers (Quebec) required
Insurance / Assurance / Reassurance - prior AMF licensing required
Trust / Fiducie / Fiduciaire / Loan and Investment - prior AMF or other financial-services regulator approval required
University / Universite / College / Institut - prior approval of the Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur required
Order / Ordre / Barreau / Avocat / Notaire / Architecte / Comptable - prior approval of the relevant Quebec professional order required
Royal / Reine / Gouvernement / Ministere / Agence / Police / Armee / Canada / Quebec - words implying Crown, governmental, or municipal association require ministerial or royal assent
Any word that is obscene, discriminatory, contrary to public order, or that creates confusion with a name already registered, reserved, or pending in the REQ enterprise register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The REQ name-clearance procedure begins with a NUANS name-search request on the REQ portal; upon approval the registrar issues an attestation of validity (approval) that remains valid for 90 days, during which the articles of incorporation must be filed. No statutory extension of the attestation exists; upon expiry, a fresh NUANS search and new attestation are required. If the proposed name is refused, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration (demande de revision) with the Directeur general des registres within 30 days of notification under the LPLE, attaching the original rejection notice and a response to each stated objection; the registrar must review the request and render a decision. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Cour superieure du Quebec within 60 days. As a practical alternative, the applicant may file a modified name with a new NUANS search at the statutory tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted, with conditions. A QBCA corporation must at all times maintain a registered office with a real physical street address in Quebec (QBCA s. 191). A registered-agent service providing a Quebec street address, mail acceptance, and mail forwarding, without the corporation actually operating at that location, is accepted by the REQ for zero-employee digital-only publishing entities. However, corporate tax residency under Section 250 of the Income Tax Act (Canada) is determined by central management and control; a non-resident shareholder/director group using only a Quebec virtual office will not, by itself, create Canadian tax residency if actual board decisions occur abroad. Canadian banks underwriting the corporate account for AdMob and AppLovin payouts may require disclosure of the operational address and may condition approval on a physical operating presence or a Canadian director.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate - the REQ conducts virtually no unannounced physical inspections of registered offices outside of tenancy-address verification where mail is returned; the quantified inspection risk for a compliant, small-payroll digital publishing corporation is under 2% per fiscal year. Revenue Quebec (GST/QST and corporate tax) field-visit risk is estimated at 3-5% over a five-year cycle, primarily triggered by irregular cross-border advertising-network inflows, related-party invoices, or missing annual declarations. The registered office may be visited during such a tax audit, and the corporation must be able to produce the statutory registers, including the UBO register, within a reasonable period at that office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and name-clearance request through the REQ
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; CAD 46.90 plus applicable taxes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of incorporation filed online through the REQ, including enterprise registration and issuance of the certificate of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec / Ministere du Travail, de l'Emploi et de la Solidarite sociale
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory QBCA incorporation tariff: CAD 348 online, CAD 403 paper filing, inclusive of the enterprise registration filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial declaration and UBO declaration filing with the REQ (registration of directors, registered office, and ultimate beneficiaries)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Included in the incorporation filing fee under the LPLE; no additional statutory levy

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Attestation of validity of the proposed corporate name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No additional charge when requested together with the NUANS approval under REQ service tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille of foreign director and UBO identity documents in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and designated competent authority of the origin state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and apostille tariffs; range USD 80-150 per individual batch

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign corporate and identity documents (OCTAQ-certified translator)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: OCTAQ-certified translator or Chambre des notaires du Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CAD 25-40 per page; estimated 3-5 pages for passport, address proof, and corporate certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec legal counsel flat fee for drafting articles of incorporation, initial corporate resolutions, statutory registers, UBO register, and shareholder consents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a single-incorporator QBCA private corporation: CAD 700-1,500 flat fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office virtual service in Quebec (street address, mail acceptance and forwarding) - first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CAD 250-400 per year for non-commercial digital-entity virtual office services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and Canadian sanctions screening package for directors and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance data vendor (e.g., Refinitiv World-Check, LexisNexis, Dow Jones)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CAD 50-100 for one-time batch screening of up to five individuals

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening and underwriting compliance package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Canadian chartered bank or US-acquiring partner bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory account-opening fee; QBCA imposes no minimum capital requirement; bank underwriting may require a CAD 0-2,000 initial deposit or a Canadian-resident director as a condition of account approval

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1), ss. 11, 15, 19, 20, 27, 111, 122 and 125; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, individuals, partnerships and legal persons (CQLR c P-45), s. 14
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Quebec City, Quebec, Canada
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) submitted with the initial declaration of registration (déclaration d'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; one or more common shares without par value issued for nominal consideration are sufficient. No escrow account, bank certificate, or capital deposit is required before incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription agreement between the Corporation and the founding shareholder for 1,000 common shares without par value be approved, at the agreed nominal consideration, and that the directors issue such shares fully paid and non-assessable; RESOLVED, that the registered office be fixed at [street address], [municipality], Quebec, and that the Secretary file all legal publicity notices with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; RESOLVED, that [name], [name], and [name] be appointed respectively Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual meeting, with authority to execute banking, regulatory, and operational instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name search and priority reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ 'Services en ligne' portal. The proposed name must comply with the QBCA and the Regulation respecting names; if a personal name is used, include a distinctive element. Submit the name reservation application and pay the priority fee. The reservation is valid for 90 days and may be renewed if necessary. Proceed to incorporation within that window or adopt a numbered name, e.g. '[NEQ] Canada Inc.'
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name in French or bilingual form
Statement of primary activity (ISIC 5820 software publishing)
Applicant contact details
Name reservation fee payment record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, the Registrar gives the obstacle; amend the name with a new distinctive denomination and refile online. The fee is not refunded. Alternatively, apply for a numbered company and register that name as a trade name later.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and submission of articles of incorporation and legal publicity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — corporation constitution filing module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles in French or bilingual form on the official model form. If incorporating by a natural person, sign online using a secure digital credential; paper filing with wet signature is also accepted. The articles may create one class of unlimited common shares without par value and, if desired, restrictions on share transfers. Submit the initial legal publicity declaration showing the registered office address, directors, and officers. Pay the official filing fee, presently approximately USD 240 equivalent. The certificate of incorporation is issued electronically when the file is complete.
required_dossiers: Completed articles of incorporation on the QBCA Schedule A model
Initial legal publicity declaration
Name reservation certificate if a nominal legal name is used
Consent of each director to act as director
Registered office address and, if applicable, landlord's written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is refused, the Registrar's refusal letter identifies missing sections or signature deficiencies; correct the articles, re-upload, and resubmit within 30 days to preserve the priority date. For paper filings, re-attest signatures before submission at the REQ counter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) integrated business registration service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Quebec enterprise electronic registration service to activate the NEQ and open the corporate file with Revenu Québec. Apply for GST/HST and QST registration. If the corporation has employees, register for source deductions and payroll remittances with the CRA and create a CNESST employer account in Quebec. Select NAICS 511210. The CRA corporate tax account is generally created automatically through the REQ-CRA data exchange after the certificate of incorporation is issued.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Quebec enterprise number (NEQ)
Business and mailing addresses
Directors' dates of birth and residential addresses
Description of hyper-casual game publishing activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account is not created automatically, contact the Revenu Québec business integration support line with the REQ certificate and director identifiers. For late GST/HST or QST registration, file a request for penalty relief under CRA and Revenu Québec administrative guidelines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational meeting, by-laws and first board resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation — internal corporate governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting of the directors within a reasonable time after incorporation. Adopt framework by-laws respecting the fiscal year, banking, quorum, and share transfer formalities. Pass the pro-forma first board resolution approving the share subscription, confirming the registered office, and appointing the Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer. Issue the subscribed shares against lawful consideration, deliver share certificates, and update the share register and minute book. A written resolution signed by all directors has the same effect as a board meeting.
required_dossiers: Notice and agenda of the organizational meeting
Framework by-laws
Pro-forma first board resolution as set out in the legal framework above
Subscription agreement and evidence of payment
Consents to act as officers and directors
Share certificates and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If unanimity is not obtained, reconvene the meeting after proper notice and proceed by majority. If any director or officer resigns or is unavailable, appoint a replacement by resolution of the board or shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal occupancy and office fire safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permits and inspection service of the relevant Quebec municipality or borough; local fire safety inspector
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a certificate of occupancy (certificat d'occupation) for the leased premises used as an office. Provide the lease, floor plan, and employee count. Arrange a fire safety inspection confirming compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code: fire extinguishers, unobstructed exits, emergency lighting, and illuminated exit signs. This is an administrative clearance only; no sectoral operating license is required for publishing lightweight ad-monetized mobile games.
required_dossiers: Municipal certificate of occupancy application form
Office lease agreement
Floor plan with room schedule
Certificate of incorporation and NEQ
Fire prevention equipment layout
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality requires zoning conformation or structural verification, provide an architect's or engineer's certification and amend the application. If the fire inspector identifies deficiencies, install the required appliances at the landlord's cost and schedule a reinspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental impact classification and compliance confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — regional authorization branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that hyper-casual game publishing under ISIC 5820 has no listed activity under Schedule B of the Quebec Environmental Quality Act and is therefore exempt from environmental impact assessment and environmental authorization. Prepare a short classification memorandum and retain it in the corporate compliance file. If the office includes a server room or emergency generator, ensure exhaust and fuel storage thresholds remain below provincial regulatory ceilings and arrange separate collection of electronic waste.
required_dossiers: Activity classification memorandum
Office lease or premises description
Electronic waste and residue management agreement if applicable
None if no environmental permit is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MELCCFP requests additional verification, supply the classification memorandum and premises documentation. For unforeseen generator or HVAC emissions, file the applicable declaration under the Quebec Clean Air Regulation and obtain any municipal exhaust permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no Quebec industrial licensing authority exercises jurisdiction over ISIC 5820 software publishing for hyper-casual games; municipal zoning and fire authorities apply to the office premises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal certificate of occupancy (certificat d'occupation); no sector-specific operating license or gaming publication permit is required in Quebec

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — software publishing (ISIC 5820) is not listed in the mandatory environmental impact assessment categories under the Quebec Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2); no environmental authorization is triggered by office-based game publishing activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, industrial VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation from the licensed activity. Office operations must comply with municipal sewer and waste-sorting bylaws. If emergency generators are installed, exhaust must meet the applicable thresholds of the Quebec Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c Q-2, r. 4.1) and fuel storage must comply with provincial petroleum equipment regulations. Electronic waste must be managed under the Quebec Residual Materials Management Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification, structural load confirmation, and workplace attendance clearance are required for the leased office. The local fire service must inspect for portable extinguishers, unobstructed exits, emergency lighting, and illuminated exit signage under the Quebec Fire Safety Code (CQLR c S-3.1, r. 3). The Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) employer registration and a workplace accident-prevention program are required for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Provincial: Revenu Quebec - registration portal via https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/; Registraire des entreprises du Quebec for the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate as a business corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act (federal) or Quebec Business Corporations Act; obtain Articles of Incorporation and, for Quebec, the NEQ. Step 2 - Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA via BRO, Form RC1, or telephone; the BN is the statutory TIN and base for GST/HST program account (RT), federal corporate income tax (T2), and payroll (RP). Step 3 - Register with Revenu Quebec for the QST account (NR program), Quebec corporate income tax (CO-17), and Quebec payroll/QPIP accounts; the QST registration number generally follows the pattern 1234567890 TQ 0001. Step 4 - Complete the joint federal-Quebec new business registration questionnaire to synchronize CRA and Revenu Quebec accounts. Step 5 - File T2 and CO-17 returns within six months of fiscal year-end. Non-resident shareholders are permitted without minimum capital; the corporation is deemed resident under ITA s. 250 and taxed under Part I of the Income Tax Act and Part I of the Quebec Taxation Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; a business corporation is a separate resident taxpayer on worldwide income. Available elections: (1) associated-corporation elections and Small Business Deduction allocation agreements for Canadian-controlled private corporations under ITA Part I and the Quebec Taxation Act; (2) election to waive the Small Business Deduction; (3) hybrid mismatch notional-account elections and BEPS Action 2 adjustments as codified in the Income Tax Act; (4) functional currency election (ITA s. 261); (5) foreign affiliate exempt-surplus and designated-surplus elections under ITA s. 5907 and Part LIX regulations; (6) non-resident-owned investment corporation status is not applicable given active game-publishing business.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual indirect tax system: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act administered by CRA, plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) under Title I of the Quebec Taxation Act administered by Revenu Quebec; functionally a VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 for GST (small-supplier threshold on total worldwide taxable supplies, measured per calendar quarter or four consecutive quarters); CAD 30,000 for QST (identical small-supplier threshold). Mandatory registration once either threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration permitted below threshold. Non-resident digital-supplier simplified GST/QST registration applies to foreign platforms supplying Canadian consumers, but is not required for the resident game publisher itself.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, government pre-approval, or digital stamping mandate exists in Canada or Quebec. Invoices must state the supplier's BN, GST/QST registration numbers, invoice date, vendor/receiver identity, description, tax base, and tax amounts. Records must be retained in readable electronic form for six years under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Tax Administration Act. Mandatory electronic filing applies to corporate income tax and GST/HST/QST returns for registrants exceeding revenue thresholds; Peppol-based B2B e-invoicing is optional under the Pan-Canadian B2B e-Invoicing framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Excise Tax Act s. 23 and Schedule VI Part V, supplies of services (including advertising and ad-network mediation) and intangible personal property (game software licenses, in-app digital content) made to non-resident recipients are zero-rated where the recipient is not receiving the supply in Canada. The QST zero-rating mirrors the GST under the Quebec Taxation Act. For hyper-casual ad-monetized games, zero-rating applies where: (1) advertising inventory is supplied to non-resident ad networks or advertisers such as AdMob and AppLovin; (2) in-app purchases are made by non-resident users substantiated by at least two non-conflicting indicators of non-residency (foreign payment method, foreign IP address, foreign app store territory, foreign address); and (3) the corporation does not supply or promote the service for consumption in Canada. In-app revenues sourced from Canada or Quebec consumers remain taxable at the combined 14.975% rate (GST 5% plus QST 9.975%).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) - required for physical goods only; for digital downloads and ad services the functional equivalent is the digital export invoice and IP licensing/assignment record
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill - applicable only where tangible promotional items or physical media accompany the digital supply; retained as evidence in mixed transactions
Inward Remittance Certificate - bank credit advices, SWIFT records, and e-wallet settlement statements from AdMob and AppLovin demonstrating offshore currency inflow
Executed service and license agreements with non-resident advertisers or ad networks specifying place of supply and recipient jurisdiction
Platform payout statements (AdMob payments report, AppLovin dashboard settlement report) evidencing non-resident counterparties and foreign-origin revenue
Export ledger with per-transaction zero-rating narratives and the corporation's written export policy
Non-residency evidence bundle: foreign business registration numbers, foreign TINs, bank account jurisdiction, and user IP geolocation data for digital in-app sales
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess GST/QST within 4 years of filing (extended indefinitely for misrepresentation, fraud, or waiver); income tax reassessment generally applies within 3-4 years by entity type. Improper export zero-rating triggers retrospective clawback of uncollected net tax plus compound daily interest at the prescribed rate. Civil penalties include: ITA s. 163(2) penalty of 50% of income tax avoided for false statements or omissions; Excise Tax Act s. 280 failure-to-file penalty of 5% of net tax plus 5% per complete month (maximum 12 months); Excise Tax Act s. 285 gross-negligence penalty of 25% of net tax (minimum CAD 100) for knowingly false statements; and mirror penalties under the Quebec Taxation Act and Tax Administration Act. Missing remittance or platform payout evidence within the 180-day repatriation benchmark raises audit risk and may result in full clawback of zero-rated input tax credits and net tax. Note: Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the benchmark reflects CRA administrative practice, and accrued receivables are reportable on the accrual basis regardless of settlement timing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime with full current account convertibility under the Bank of Canada Act. Capital account transactions, including equity investments and profit remittances, generally permit free repatriation subject to prior notification for non-resident investments above CAD 100 million and mandatory FATCA/CRS reporting. Profit remittance hurdles include 15-25% dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No central bank surrender obligation applies to most digital service or ad revenue exports. Repatriation occurs at market rates upon bank receipt of commercial invoices, proof of delivery, and AML documentation. Export permits under the Export and Import Permit Act are required solely for restricted goods; otherwise, banks process conversions freely with FINTRAC compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility; offshore EMIs require MSB registration with FINTRAC under PCMLTFA, imposing licensing, capital, and cross-border compliance burdens incompatible with hyper-casual gaming payout volumes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Video KYC and remote opening permitted for accounts under CAD 100,000; directors and signatories must complete in-person or verified video interviews for higher-value or elevated-risk accounts. Quebec branch visits required for initial setup in select cases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership >25% or shell company structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation, articles of association, shareholder register, beneficial ownership declaration, and source of wealth attestation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned jurisdiction links or adverse media
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence report, legal opinion on compliance, transaction history, and source of funds proof

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 to Canadian bank accounts with purpose codes 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. Verification mandates share subscription agreements, board resolutions, incorporation documents, and source of funds proof to satisfy FINTRAC and CRA requirements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements route via SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit for structured trade finance. Ad revenue disbursements utilize licensed processors with correspondent banking in USD or EUR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for a Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual anniversary of the corporation's date of registration with REQ.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a REQ penalty (approximately CAD 25); continued default for one or more annual declaration cycles can trigger a notice of default and may lead to administrative dissolution/cancellation of the enterprise registration after the prescribed delay.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (if the corporation is CBCA-incorporated and operating in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the annual anniversary date of incorporation as shown in the federal certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may lead to a notice of dissolution; continued failure for two consecutive years can result in administrative dissolution under the CBCA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth month after the corporation's taxation year-end; June 30 for a December 31 year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month of arrears up to 12 months; repeated default may trigger director liability, denial of loss carryback adjustments, and interest on unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17 / T2-CO17)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within six months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year; the fiscal year must correspond to the federal taxation year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus interest at the prescribed rate, with an additional 1% monthly late-filing penalty; failure to file may also affect objections, refunds, and provincial loss carries.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private corporations under the Quebec Business Corporations Act are not subject to a revenue- or asset-based statutory audit threshold. An auditor must be appointed at each annual meeting unless all shareholders, including non-voting shareholders, consent to dispense with the auditor for the year. Public issuers, banks, and other regulated corporations cannot waive the audit requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for public companies and certain regulated entities; private Quebec corporations may consistently apply IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Financial statements prepared for shareholders must follow the chosen generally accepted accounting principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration must confirm and update the ultimate beneficiary information required under Quebec's legal publicity regime, including any individual with direct or indirect control or ownership of 25% or more of voting rights or equity value. Share transfers affecting beneficial ownership must be reflected in the corporate share-transfer register and, where applicable, in the federal Register of Individuals with Significant Control within 15 days of the change. The annual declaration is the required annual mechanism for updating registry-level beneficial ownership in Quebec.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (articles, by-laws, minutes and resolutions of directors and shareholders)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control / Ultimate Beneficiaries (where applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$100–US$400 per year for registered office representation, annual declaration preparation, and filing-agent compliance services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$8,000–US$20,000 for a full statutory-quality audit of a small or medium private corporation; US$1,500–US$4,500 for a review or compilation engagement when the audit is waived.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate income tax rate: 15%. Quebec general corporate income tax rate: 11.5%. Combined general rate: 26.5%. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a federal rate of 9% and a Quebec rate of 3.2% on eligible active business income within the applicable business limit, producing a combined rate of approximately 12.2%, subject to eligibility, business-limit allocation, associated-corporation rules, and income-type restrictions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal and Quebec small-business deductions may reduce tax on eligible active business income. Federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development credits, Quebec R&D tax credits, and certain multimedia, digital-media, and interactive-production incentives may apply only if statutory technical, expenditure, labour, ownership, certification, and filing conditions are satisfied. No general tax holiday applies to an ordinary hyper-casual mobile-game publisher. Dividend tax integration, foreign tax credits, capital cost allowance, and loss utilization may reduce current tax but are not rate holidays.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including applicable schedules and forms, filed electronically through CRA Corporation Internet Filing or CRA My Business Account. Quebec CO-17 Déclaration de revenus des sociétés, including applicable schedules, filed electronically through Revenu Québec transmission services or an authorized tax preparer. A corporation carrying on business in Quebec generally has both federal and Quebec corporate income tax filing obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; tax instalments generally monthly or quarterly depending on statutory eligibility and prior-year tax liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Both the T2 and CO-17 are generally due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any balance is generally payable within two months after year-end. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally have three months to pay its balance if statutory conditions are satisfied, although the return remains due within six months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, corporation type, tax year, incorporation jurisdiction, fiscal period, mailing address, principal business activity, and ownership or control information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Canadian corporation's legal and tax identity. Identify non-resident shareholders, parent entities, foreign permanent establishments, and changes of control accurately. A Canadian subsidiary remains resident in Canada unless a valid treaty residence position applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ownership, associated corporations, control, and corporate structure information relevant to private-corporation status and business-limit allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign control and associated corporations. Do not claim Canadian-controlled private corporation status where non-residents control the corporation, directly or indirectly, or where statutory de facto control rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income to income for tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, tax adjustments, reserves, capital gains, and other permanent or temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude book deductions that are not deductible under Canadian law. Separately identify foreign exchange, shareholder, related-party, royalty, interest, stock-based compensation, and capital expenditure adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation and utilization of non-capital losses, net capital losses, restricted farm losses, and other applicable loss pools.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply acquisition-of-control, continuity-of-business, same-business, and streaming rules. Losses must not be used merely because a foreign parent or new investor acquired the Canadian corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance, depreciable property, additions, dispositions, recapture, terminal losses, and shareholder information where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalize qualifying software, servers, development equipment, and other depreciable property according to Canadian classes. Distinguish internally developed game intellectual property, acquired IP, ordinary development costs, and current advertising expenditure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable small-business schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the federal small-business deduction and related business-limit computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim the small-business deduction unless the corporation is eligible. Foreign-controlled corporations generally cannot claim Canadian-controlled private corporation benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 31 and related foreign-tax-credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign business income, foreign non-business income, foreign taxes paid, and foreign tax credit calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support each foreign tax credit with foreign assessments, withholding certificates, contracts, and income attribution. Prevent double relief where an amount is also deducted or relieved under a treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 44 and related R&D forms
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal SR&ED expenditures and investment tax credit claims, where eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain project-level technical narratives, hypotheses, experiments, time records, payroll allocation, contractor documentation, and expenditure tracing. Routine game coding, content production, debugging, and commercial development are not automatically SR&ED.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party and non-arm's-length transaction disclosure. Form T106 is required for reportable transactions with non-residents where the statutory reporting conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border management fees, development services, advertising services, IP licences, royalties, loans, guarantees, cost-sharing, and intercompany settlements. Reconcile T106 amounts to the general ledger, financial statements, transfer-pricing documentation, and withholding-tax slips.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Quebec CO-17 Schedule 1 and taxable-income reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable-income computation, accounting-to-tax reconciliation, deductions, losses, and Quebec-specific adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Quebec adjustments separately from federal computations. Apportion income where the corporation operates in more than one jurisdiction and maintain payroll, revenue, and establishment records supporting Quebec allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Quebec CO-17 Schedule 7 and related tax-credit schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec loss utilization, refundable and non-refundable tax credits, R&D incentives, and eligible digital or multimedia production credits where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm certification and Quebec labour-content requirements before claiming media or digital-production incentives. Maintain employee location, subcontractor, production, and ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indirect-tax returns separate from T2 and CO-17. Registration, collection, place-of-supply, platform, digital-service, and input-tax-credit rules may apply to game sales, in-app purchases, advertising, and subscriptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine whether the Canadian entity, foreign platform, app store, or payment intermediary is responsible for GST/HST or QST collection. Preserve platform statements and distinguish advertising revenue from consumer digital sales.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T4, T5, NR4, RL-1, RL-3, and related slips
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payroll, dividends, interest, royalties, and other reportable payment slips and information returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue appropriate slips for employee compensation, dividends, and Canadian-source amounts paid to non-residents. Match slips, remittances, and general-ledger accounts to avoid withholding discrepancies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late-filing penalty is generally 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% of unpaid tax for each complete month late, generally capped at 12 months, with higher repeat-failure penalties. Quebec generally applies a 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month, subject to statutory limits and additional penalties for failure to file electronically or to provide required information. Interest accrues on unpaid balances and instalment deficiencies at prescribed rates. Gross-negligence, false-statement, repeated-failure, and evasion penalties may apply in addition to late-filing penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on taxable dividends paid or credited to a non-resident, subject to reduction under an applicable income tax treaty. Common treaty rates are 15% for qualifying portfolio holdings and 5% for qualifying corporate holdings, but the applicable treaty, ownership percentage, holding period, limitation-on-benefits provisions, beneficial-ownership test, and anti-avoidance rules must be verified.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain and retain a valid CRA Form NR301, NR302, or NR303, or equivalent documentary evidence, before applying a reduced treaty rate. Confirm the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, entity status, ownership and control, limitation-on-benefits eligibility, and absence of conduit arrangements. Apply the reduced rate at payment or credit, remit withholding by the 15th day of the following month, file the applicable NR4 information return by the last day of March following the calendar year, and issue NR4 slips. If treaty eligibility is uncertain, withhold at 25% and seek a refund or competent-authority relief where available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% on Canadian-source royalties and interest paid or credited to non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Treaty royalty rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, frequently 10%, depending on the treaty and royalty category. Treaty interest rates commonly range from 0% to 15%, frequently 10%; certain arm's-length interest payments, including many Canada-United States qualifying interest payments, may be exempt. Software, copyright, trademark, patent, know-how, advertising, platform, and technical-service payments require source, characterization, beneficial-ownership, and treaty analysis. Failure to withhold does not eliminate the payer's assessment exposure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not use a simple statutory Local File/Master File threshold equivalent to all OECD jurisdictions. Under Income Tax Act section 247, contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is required to support arm's-length pricing for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions. Form T106 reporting generally applies where the aggregate reportable transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1,000,000 or other statutory reporting conditions are met. CRA may request documentation, which generally must be provided within three months. Canadian entities subject to the OECD country-by-country reporting regime may have additional CbC reporting obligations, generally based on consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM), commonly analyzed in Canada through a transactional net margin approach
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to some offshore jurisdictions. Substance is assessed through the Income Tax Act transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, treaty residence and beneficial-ownership principles, purpose and abuse analysis, and judicial doctrines concerning sham transactions and legal relationships. The corporation should maintain Canadian decision-making, employees or qualified contractors, control over game development and IP risks, board governance, commercial contracts, bank accounts, accounting records, and evidence that intercompany services and IP arrangements reflect actual functions, assets, and risks.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting revenue, inflating development or advertising expenses, creating fictitious invoices, concealing app-store or advertising-platform receipts, manipulating shareholder loans, or filing materially false T2 or CO-17 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil reassessment of tax, interest, gross-negligence penalties generally equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the understated tax or overstated credit, and possible prosecution under the Income Tax Act. Tax evasion can result in fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to five years, subject to the charged offence and court determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face prosecution for personal participation, authorization, acquiescence, or wilful blindness. Corporate tax debt does not ordinarily become director debt solely because of office, but personal criminal liability, civil penalties, restitution, and prosecution remain possible. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax sanction but may arise from bail, court orders, immigration consequences, or enforcement of a criminal sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Remit Payroll, GST/HST, QST, or Part XIII Withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using source deductions or non-resident withholding for working capital, failing to deduct withholding from dividends, royalties, interest, or management fees, or failing to remit amounts collected from customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the unremitted amount, interest, penalties, director-liability exposure, and potential criminal prosecution. Part XIII withholding assessments can include the required tax plus interest and penalties. GST/HST and QST amounts collected and not remitted may be treated as trust amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable under federal and Quebec statutory provisions for unremitted source deductions and certain trust amounts if statutory due-diligence defences are unavailable. Personal assets may be pursued after corporate recovery steps. Imprisonment requires criminal prosecution and conviction; a travel ban is not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive foreign management fees, royalties, advertising fees, development fees, or interest; shifting valuable game IP to a low-tax affiliate without arm's-length compensation; or using unsupported cost-plus or revenue-share arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment under Income Tax Act section 247, denial of deductions, income inclusion, interest, penalties generally equal to 10% of the adjustment in qualifying circumstances, and possible secondary withholding-tax consequences. Repeated or abusive arrangements may trigger GAAR or treaty anti-abuse provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not ordinarily personally liable merely because a pricing adjustment is made. Personal exposure may arise for knowing participation in fraud, false statements, obstruction, or deliberate tax evasion. CRA may assess penalties against the corporation and pursue responsible individuals criminally.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Sham, or Artificial IP Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Canadian corporation with no real business activity, employees, control, development functions, or commercial risk while booking profits, IP ownership, or treaty benefits in Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, recharacterization of transactions, loss of treaty benefits, GAAR assessment, withholding-tax reassessment, transfer-pricing adjustments, interest, and civil penalties. Beneficial-ownership and residence claims may be rejected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal exposure where they knowingly participated in sham documentation, fraud, or evasion. Corporate separateness is generally respected for legitimate operations, but it does not protect individuals from criminal conduct, statutory director liability, or fraudulent-transfer consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Proceeds of Crime, and Sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained funds, disguising related-party transfers as advertising or development payments, processing sanctioned-party payments, falsifying beneficial-ownership information, or using payment processors to conceal the source or destination of funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential FINTRAC compliance measures, administrative monetary penalties, transaction restrictions, criminal prosecution under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act or Criminal Code, forfeiture, and sanctions-related penalties. Corporate and individual consequences depend on the conduct and applicable regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally prosecuted for knowing participation, counselling, aiding, abetting, or directing unlawful transactions. Conviction can result in fines, forfeiture, imprisonment, and court-imposed travel restrictions. A travel ban is not automatic solely from an AML finding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper SR&ED or Quebec Digital-Media Credit Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming routine game design, ordinary coding, marketing, content production, or subcontractor costs as qualifying R&D or digital-media expenditure without technical uncertainty, eligible labour, certification, or Quebec nexus.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial or clawback of credits, reassessment of tax, interest, gross-negligence penalties, preparer penalties where applicable, and potential prosecution for knowingly false claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for deliberate false statements, fraud, or criminal participation. Ordinary corporate overclaiming without personal misconduct generally does not pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Records, Beneficial Ownership, and Filing Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain prescribed corporate records, beneficial-ownership information, accounting books, transfer-pricing evidence, board approvals, or supporting documents for related-party payments and tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties, filing penalties, denial of deductions or treaty relief, audit reassessments, compliance orders, and possible offences under federal or Quebec corporate, tax, and anti-money-laundering legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face statutory fines or prosecution for authorizing non-compliance and may lose the ability to rely on a due-diligence defence. Personal imprisonment or travel restrictions require applicable criminal proceedings or court orders and are not automatic consequences of a recordkeeping deficiency.
